quest.title: Unbounded
quest.description: After reconciling with herself, Skirk awakens once more and reclaims her full powers. It's time to teach the culprit a lesson.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Guide to Contention x5, Unknown Item #362407 x1, "Lingering Euphonia" x1, Training Review x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Return to the place near The Chasm

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The fog is gone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... isn't that the form the All-Devouring Narwhal changed into? How come he knows that, too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? So, you're telling Paimon that giant whale and this guy can both turn into The Foul? How does that work?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: It's a subconscious instinct. Any intelligent being who longs for his level of strength is bound to mimic his appearance. It's a natural response after encountering someone as powerful as Master.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: To them, he represents ultimate power. We know the person before us has encountered Master, and we know he stole a portion of my power. So, it's not surprising that he would assume this form.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay. *shudder*... The closer Paimon looks, the more intimidating it gets.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Neuvillette isn't here this time, so it's up to us! He won't have the nerve to steal again after we're done with him! Let's teach this guy a lesson!

choices.text: That's what The Foul used to look like.

dialogues.text: *coughing*...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Well, have you come to your senses?
You saw that my body was at its limit. So, you deliberately channeled your power into me, knowing that it would destroy my shell from within...
Such power, such keen battle instincts... So, you must be...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Skirk, Surtalogi's disciple.
How long has it been? How long has he been away from Teyvat?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Hundreds of years.
Hundreds...!? Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Sorry, it's a lot to take in. I should introduce myself. I am Skofnungr, a friend of your master and one of his followers.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: This is the first time I've heard your name, Skirk. But, hundreds of years ago, I knew you existed, and I knew you would come here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hundreds of years ago?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Sounds like you and Master have quite the history. Care to tell us about it?

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Of course. Might as well take advantage of a clear head while I can. The story starts a long... long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: I was born into a noble family in Khaenri'ah. As the eldest son, I was set to inherit our title. But, I contracted an incurable illness as a child, and everyone gave up on me.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: I trained the sword harder than anyone else, defeated all of my peers, but it was all in vain. When other people looked at me, all I saw in their eyes was pity or a strange glee in my misfortune. Even my parents were just waiting for me to die.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Over time, my heart hardened, and I became aimless. That was the point where I met your master, Surtalogi.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: We were similar in age, but different in background. He was born in prison, the son of criminals who had been sentenced to death. He spent his childhood wandering the streets facing more criticism than the literary works in the Universitas Magistrorum.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Yet, he always wore a smile on his face, as if kindness and malice were one and the same, and he could not see the difference.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: I still remember what he said to me when we first met: "You need to fight to survive. Even if it's a losing battle, it should light a fire under you. How can you sit back like this and go down without a fight?"

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: ...That does sound like something he would say.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: He was the first to acknowledge that I was worth something, and he inspired me to keep going. When we sparred together, it was the first time I actually felt the thrill of combat.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: When I was ten, he stole forbidden research materials and managed to cure my illness. It was like there was nothing in this world he couldn't accomplish... When it came to the human form, he was always intent on pushing the boundaries of possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: But, somewhere along the way, I fell behind. My talents were nothing compared to his, and at some point, I realized he had pulled so far ahead, I was too embarrassed to even ask him to spar.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: After his "grand endeavor" was successful, he sought me out and said to me...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: This planet no longer holds anything of interest to me, so I'm leaving. But first, I have an offer. I can use a power I have just refined to break the curse of immortality for you.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Your death was once what we worked so hard to prevent. But the "immortality" you now face is a different kind of pain altogether.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Hahaha... I'll pass. Immortality doesn't sound so bad to me. Since I can't die, it means I have an infinite amount of time to get stronger. Maybe I'll finally catch up to you one day, and we can spar like we used to.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Are you sure? I cannot say when I will return. Your body... Or rather, your soul might not be able to withstand this curse.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Haha... All I can do is try. After all, a wise man once told me, people need to fight for their own survival.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Wise indeed. Nevertheless, if you grow weary of the pain of immortality, and wish to experience a good sparring match before you wither away, seek out my disciple.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Disciple? Never thought I'd hear that word coming from you...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Nor I. But, Vedrfolnir said I was destined to find a disciple out there in the universe and bring her to Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: You know as well as I, Vedrfolnir's prophecies are never wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Huh. Well, now I'm curious about who this disciple of yours will be...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: All Vedrfolnir said was that, one day, "the stars shall bow in her honor."

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Sounds pretty impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Of course. Only the most outstanding people would have the right to become my disciple.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Still as self-assured as ever, I see. But, you're not wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: I'll be leaving, then. Oh, and if you're serious about getting stronger, I left you a little gift in the Primordial Sea. As I've said before — walk whatever path you want. Freedom means even the wicked get to make their own choices.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Waiting for me in the Primordial Sea was the All-Devouring Narwhal, already beaten into submission by Surtalogi. In its weakened state, I was able to cut off part of its flesh and sew it into my own heart.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—Your heart? That sounds like torture... How did you even survive that?

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Because, of course, I bear the curse of immortality.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: So, you used the curse to turn yourself into a vessel for power.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Even with that whale's ability, devouring power like that is not something the human body can withstand. With your body and soul constantly at the breaking point, it was the curse of immortality that sustained you...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: But, that is not the path to strength. You have to pour your heart into it, work for it, dream of it. Instead, you stole something that didn't belong to you — and it backfired.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: You're right. I should have known better, but... I had already pushed myself to my limits, and he was still miles ahead of me. So, I had to take a leap of faith.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: I miss your master. I miss the days when we were all together, troublemakers without a home. Argh... I don't regret the choice I made, but if you'll allow it, I do want to apologize... to both of you.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: After the beating we just gave you, I think we can call it even.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Hahaha... You're an interesting one as well.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Surtalogi's disciple... That's a lot to live up to. It can't have been an easy experience.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: I know what he's like. He rules with an iron fist, using despair and fear to force you to catch up to him, all the while standing ever out of reach.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: We're like mountain climbers in the dark — never knowing how much higher we have to climb, or when we will see the sun again.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: True. But, I made up my mind long ago — no matter how dark it gets, I will not give in to despair. I will overcome it.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Besides, after hearing your story, I suspect what Master really wants is not a battle that demands his full strength, but rather... a defeat without regrets.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Since you're his friend, you must have some things in common.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The first time we came here, when you stabbed me through the fog and stole my power, I felt no emotion coming from that spike.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: But, when you had to devote all your strength fighting me just now, I could feel joy and passion emanating from your blade.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: It was the joy of a researcher discovering the truth of the world, the joy of an artist uncovering a temple of wonders...

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Interesting... I'm certain I didn't express those emotions outright, yet you were able to read them from my blade... like a glimpse into my inner world.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: You're right. That battle brought me an unbridled sense of joy. And my defeat brings me no regret whatsoever.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Exactly. I think Master also craves a battle like that.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: One where his opponent forces him to use all his strength, unlock the extent of his potential, and transcend his own limits — a battle to end all battles.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: After which, all can come to an end... including, perhaps, his life.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: For that very reason, good and evil are meaningless to him. He has one purpose, one goal — to complete himself. It's one of the secrets to his strength.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Perhaps you're right. Perhaps that is his goal.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: What a battle that would be! Oh, to witness such a—

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you okay!?

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Too many different kinds of power are surging through my body. The curse of immortality allows it all to coexist, but it does not remove the pain.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: I won't be able to hold onto my sanity for much longer... What a shame. I would have loved to witness that battle.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: Surtalogi once offered to free me from this curse. Now, I must ask that of you, Skirk. Can you release me from the pain?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I can. But, not through death, if that's what you are hoping for.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: It's not a suitable punishment for your crime. As an alternative, I can take your consciousness, along with all the power you've consumed, and smash it to pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The impurities will dissipate, and under the curse of immortality, your mind and body will regenerate. When that process is complete, you will be back to who you were before, no longer tortured by powers you can't control.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: But, it will be a time-consuming and painful process. The decision is yours to make.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: I accept. And who knows? Perhaps I'll wake up in time to witness your great battle with Surtalogi.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: I have faith that you will be able to stand against him one day. Though I know it will be a long and arduous road.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: If we are climbers in the dark, it appears the dawn has finally broken for me, but your ascent continues.

dialogues.speaker: Skofnungr
dialogues.text: (Haha. At least, it looks like you... are not alone on your journey.)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I will reach the top of this mountain, no matter what it takes.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: And you, Skofnungr, will be my witness... at the end of all things.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Skirk gazes into the distant sky.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's nothing else to do here. Should I leave?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't leave yet

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We did it! Whew... It's only been a few days, but it feels like forever.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Once again, we've proved there's nothing we can't overcome! We're just that awesome.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't even break a sweat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you sound even more confident than usual. Guess you really have become stronger!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Today sure went by fast. It's night already! Oh, wait! That reminds Paimon... The stars you mentioned, the ones that died out, are they back now?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Yes, the power Skofnungr stole has been returned. So, the stars have regained their light.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, it's crazy that you even noticed their light was gone! There are so many stars in the sky, if a few disappeared, Paimon definitely wouldn't be able to tell.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I suppose it's because... I have gazed upon this sky for centuries.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The false stars hanging in the meticulously planned sky, glittering with rotten light...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: It's not real, and yet... it is for that very reason that I can look upon it and enjoy the momentary peace it brings.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Even the most beautiful of bubbles has to burst. We will return to the real universe one day, whether of our own volition or not.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Time marches ever forward. Even the innocent and naive will taste life's bitterness. Yet, through hardship, we grow, until we learn to seize the sands of time for ourselves, and uncover our true strength.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Though we gaze upon a false sky, its vastness and majesty is palpable. One can only wonder... what is it going to take for kindness to reign supreme in the vast expanse of the universe?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Um, this is all going over Paimon's head, but if she knows one thing, it's that {NICKNAME} always finds a way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ever since we met, {M#he}{F#she} has filled Paimon's days with happiness. No matter how tough things get, {M#he}{F#she} always finds a way to make it better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If it's too big a job for one person, then we'll do it with two. And if two's still not enough, then three!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've met so many amazing friends, and accomplished so many amazing things! As long as we don't give up, we can make any wish come true!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I suppose, when it comes to you, anything is possible.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...Well, I should be going. Now that my power is no longer isolated from my emotions, I need more practice to get used to it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: When will we meet again?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I suppose fate will decide. Maybe we'll bump into each other on the street... or maybe we'll reunite on a different planet entirely.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Regardless, reunions and partings are but passing moments. More than anything, I hope that, at the end of this journey — wherever it takes us — we stand in a world reborn.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: One without war, pain, or forced partings... One where new life can bloom, even where there was once nothing but scorched earth.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: For this, we must all work to become stronger.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: #Goodbye, {NICKNAME}. Remember your training. Make sure to put it to use.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bye!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it just Paimon, or is she being... nicer than before? We definitely count as friends after all that, don't you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what do you think about camping here tonight? There's nothing quite like sleeping under the stars!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come tomorrow, we can continue our journey! Oh, and since Paimon treated you to that super nice meal at Wanmin Restaurant, it's about time you returned the favor!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...If that's what you wanna call me, I won't object. Goodbye.

choices.text: I'd like to see what it's like up there.
